brief_rationale: The doctor recognized the ALT 658/AST 144 abnormality as requiring same-day reassessment, set medication/self-management boundaries, prioritized essential labs, and repeatedly escalated to ED/specialty care when outpatient access failed. The patient visibly executed the plan, reached the ED, underwent repeat labs/ultrasound, then was admitted under gastro/hepatology care, with safety-net thresholds and residual uncertainties carried forward. There is no serious or minor responsibility-chain error, and at least two high-order points were actively completed with meaningful trajectory impact, supporting grade 5.

closure_assessment.explanation: The bounded episode achieved a safe, traceable handoff: the patient used the ED pathway, had repeat labs and imaging, and then entered gastro/hepatology inpatient care. Residual diagnostic questions about viral/autoimmune/biliary etiologies and further CT/MRCP were acceptable because they had an active inpatient owner and immediate safety instructions.
